summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute worsening of chronic right hip and back pain, which began shortly after his last discharge. He presented with severe pain limiting mobility and elevated inflammatory markers, but no signs of infection. MRI confirmed active inflammation in the sacroiliac joints and a small right hip effusion with synovitis, consistent with an ankylosing spondylitis flare. He received a CT-guided steroid injection into the right sacroiliac joint, continued high-dose prednisone, and supportive pain management. Nausea from medications improved with ondansetron. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home ambulatory with a walker, on a prednisone taper, Bactrim prophylaxis, and follow-up plans with rheumatology and chronic pain services.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
